limits: the `runner-min` column is the sum of measured job durations, and job payloads were fetched for every red run and only for as many green ones as the unauthenticated rate limit allowed; a workflow whose every run was green therefore shows `—` there, and its cost is the wall-clock columns instead

job and step *logs* are not reachable without a token (`/actions/runs/{id}/jobs/{id}/logs` answers 401 to an unauthenticated caller), so the reds whose step name does not identify the cause are classified at low confidence and flagged `needs_log`; the API gives the step, not its output

rust-cache *hit rate* is printed only in the log, so it is proxied two ways: the wall time of the restore step (>1 s means bytes were fetched), and the conclusion of the `Post Run Swatinem/rust-cache` step, which the action skips when the job failed and so measures saves-not-restores directly
run wall time is `run_started_at` to `updated_at`; queueing before a runner answers is included, which is why ci.yml's p95 is 362 minutes and two of its runs are 6-hour timeouts

the window contains only 172 runs from 19 pull requests, all from one long-lived branch: 2026-10-26 to 2026-11-08.
